user.title: Solar Energy Insights
user.description: Pick the battery, the house's energy counter and Solcast. With EF-PowerOcean-TcpModbus and Solcast installed they are filled in.

data_description.battery_capacity: In Wh or kWh. While it reports none, the last value is used.
data_description.battery_reserve: The reserve in force, in %. For EF-PowerOcean-TcpModbus: Effective Battery Reserve.
data_description.house_energy: A counter of energy the house used, daily or lifetime. Its recorded hours are what the night is replayed from.
data_description.grid_power: Optional: shows when a full battery is exporting (free power).
data_description.solcast_today: The Solcast sensor for today, with its detailedForecast attribute.
data_description.charge_limit: The level charging stops at, if set below 100 %. For EF-PowerOcean-TcpModbus: Battery Charge Limit. The plan counts the highest it has been over the last day, so a limit an automation lowers for a few hours is not taken as the day's. While it has no value, the option is used.

init.title: Settings
init.description: Prices, how the night is tested, and the battery's limits. Prices only turn kWh into money; they never change the plan.

data.import_positive: Grid power is positive when importing

data_description.nights: How many recent nights the battery is tested against.
data_description.min_reserve: The lowest the inverter discharges to by itself, under any reserve.
data_description.max_power: The most the battery charges or discharges at.
data_description.round_trip: Share of stored energy that comes back out.
data_description.import_positive: Turn off if import shows as negative.
data_description.price: What a kWh bought costs, in cents.
data_description.feed_in: What a kWh exported earns, in cents.
data_description.price_entity: For a dynamic tariff: overrides the electricity price while it has a value. Its current value applies to every hour ahead; nothing is timed to cheap hours. Read as cents if its unit starts with ct, else as your currency per kWh.
data_description.feed_in_entity: Overrides the feed-in tariff while it has a value. Read as cents if its unit starts with ct, else as your currency per kWh.
data_description.outdoor_temperature: A thermometer with statistics. With it, the scenario action can add a heat pump to your last year: the heat each hour would have needed at the temperature outside.
data_description.solar_energy: A counter of what the panels made. With it, Solcast's morning forecasts are compared with what came, and a correction for this roof is used once it beats the raw forecast.
data_description.max_charge: The level the battery charges to when no entity gives it: lower it if the app stops charging below 100 %. Full means reaching it.
data_description.achievements: Score, levels, streaks, records, badges and quests, earned from your history. The first start replays the history the recorder holds.
data_description.grid_import_energy: A counter of energy bought. With the export counter, unlocks self-sufficiency, grid-free days and the badges that use them.
data_description.grid_export_energy: A counter of energy sold. Unlocks solar kept at home and export badges.
data_description.solar_power: For the peak power record, and for estimating what the feed-in cap curtailed.
data_description.feed_in_cap: The most the grid takes, as power: above it the inverter curtails solar. For EF-PowerOcean-TcpModbus: Maximum feed-in Power. Adds what would be clipped until sunset and an estimate of what was curtailed today; the estimate needs the grid power and the solar power.
data_description.array_kwp: The panels' DC size. Read from Solcast's rooftop sites, with where each one faces; set it here only if Solcast's sites do not give it.
data_description.lookback: How long a changed answer (tonight's outlook, the grid time, when the battery is full) shows what it was before and why: from 30 minutes to 2 hours.
data_description.string_roof_pv1: Which of your Solcast sites the panels on string PV1 are on. Strings on the same roof should make about the same per kWp, so the dashboard compares them with each other.
data_description.string_roof_pv2: Which of your Solcast sites the panels on string PV2 are on. Strings on the same roof should make about the same per kWp, so the dashboard compares them with each other.
data_description.string_roof_pv3: Which of your Solcast sites the panels on string PV3 are on. Strings on the same roof should make about the same per kWp, so the dashboard compares them with each other.
data_description.string_panels_pv1: How many panels are on string PV1: count them on the roof or in your installer's plan.
data_description.string_panel_w_pv1: The watts on the panels' label, for example 420. Together with the number of panels this gives string PV1's size, which the dashboard uses to compare strings fairly. Leave both empty if you don't know.
data_description.string_panels_pv2: How many panels are on string PV2: count them on the roof or in your installer's plan.
data_description.string_panel_w_pv2: The watts on the panels' label, for example 420. Together with the number of panels this gives string PV2's size, which the dashboard uses to compare strings fairly. Leave both empty if you don't know.
data_description.string_panels_pv3: How many panels are on string PV3: count them on the roof or in your installer's plan.
data_description.string_panel_w_pv3: The watts on the panels' label, for example 420. Together with the number of panels this gives string PV3's size, which the dashboard uses to compare strings fairly. Leave both empty if you don't know.
data_description.solar_from_kw: The solar power the Solar now card and the power chart give the time of, such as "1 kW of sun from ~09:35".
data_description.battery_charged_energy: A counter of energy into the battery, for its history.
data_description.battery_discharged_energy: A counter of energy out of the battery, for its history.
data_description.solcast_sites: Solcast's rooftop site sensors: the array's roofs, directions and size.
data_description.solcast_polled: When Solcast last fetched its forecast, so a forecast is judged by when it was made.
data_description.solcast_days: Solcast's forecasts for the day after tomorrow and later, in order: day 3 first.
data_description.string_power_pv1: String 1's power, for its share of the solar. Leave empty if there is no string 1.
data_description.string_power_pv2: String 2's power, for its share of the solar. Leave empty if there is no string 2.
data_description.string_power_pv3: String 3's power, for its share of the solar. Leave empty if there is no string 3.

comparisons.name: Comparisons
comparisons.description: Which strings the dashboard holds against which. Nothing here is guessed: leave a field empty and its tiles ask for it.

data_description.compare_string: The string the Roofs tiles look at on its own: what it is worth, when it helps, and how it does on dull and sunny days.
data_description.compare_against: The strings it is held against. Empty means all the others.
data_description.compare_name: Used in the tiles' titles, e.g. North roof. Empty means the string's name.
data_description.matched_strings: Strings that should make about the same per kWp, e.g. on the same roof. The Strings in step tile compares them with each other.

error.compared_with_itself: A string can't be compared against itself: take it out of "Compare it against".

data_description.name: As it should appear, for example Dishwasher.
data_description.kwh: What a usual run takes, for example 1 kWh for a dishwasher in eco mode. Used until the energy counter has recorded a run.
data_description.hours: How long a usual run lasts.
data_description.energy: The appliance's own energy counter, such as its plug's. Its recent runs give the energy and duration of a run, in place of the typical figures, and are taken out of the nights a run is added to, so tonight's run is not counted twice.

details.title: Add an appliance
details.description: An appliance to start in the sun. It gets a sensor that says when to start it so it takes the most from sun that would otherwise be exported, and one that is on while now is a good time.

data_description.name: As it should appear, for example Dishwasher.
data_description.kwh: What a usual run takes, for example 1 kWh for a dishwasher in eco mode. Used until the energy counter has recorded a run.
data_description.hours: How long a usual run lasts.
data_description.energy: The appliance's own energy counter, such as its plug's. Its recent runs give the energy and duration of a run, in place of the typical figures, and are taken out of the nights a run is added to, so tonight's run is not counted twice.

pick.title: Add an appliance
pick.description: These energy counters look like appliances. Pick one to fill in the form, or something else to start empty.

grid_even_when_full_kwh.name: From the grid even when full

grid_even_when_full_typical_kwh.name: From the grid even when full, typical night

contested_evenings.name: Evenings that could have gone either way

state.borderline: Borderline: lasts unless it is a heavy night

simulate.name: Simulate
simulate.description: The plan with an extra load started now.

without_runs.name: Without these appliances' past runs
without_runs.description: Appliance energy counters whose past runs are taken out of the replayed nights, so the run added is not counted twice.

scenario.name: Scenario
scenario.description: Your last year again, with a bigger battery or a heat pump: what you would have bought, exported and saved, per year. Days the recorder lacks are filled from recorded days with a similar sun, so the year has a winter.

heat_loss_w_per_k.name: Heat loss
heat_loss_w_per_k.description: The house's effective heat loss per degree between inside and out: the heat it used in a year over the year's degree-hours, with the sun's and the household's heat already taken off. Lower than a heat-load calculation's. 0 for no heat pump.

heating_limit_c.name: Heating limit
heating_limit_c.description: The daily mean outdoor temperature from which the house needs no heating: about 15 °C for an older house, 12 °C for a well-insulated one.

indoor_c.name: Indoor temperature
indoor_c.description: The temperature the house is heated to.

hot_water_kwh_per_day.name: Hot water
hot_water_kwh_per_day.description: Heat for hot water per day, for example 2 kWh per person.

battery_price.name: Battery price
battery_price.description: What the extra battery costs, for the years it takes to pay back.

design_flow_c.name: Design flow temperature
design_flow_c.description: The heating water's temperature on the coldest day the heating is designed for.

design_outdoor_c.name: Design outdoor temperature
design_outdoor_c.description: The coldest day the heating is designed for, for example −12 °C.

heat_pump_kw.name: Heat pump size
heat_pump_kw.description: The most heat the heat pump gives. Above it, a heating rod adds the rest. Empty: always enough.

rated_cop.name: Rated COP
rated_cop.description: The datasheet's COP at A2/W35. Empty: an average heat pump.

hot_water_at_noon.name: Hot water in the sun
hot_water_at_noon.description: Heat the hot water in the day's sunniest hours instead of through the day.

gas_price.name: Gas price
gas_price.description: What a kWh of gas costs, to compare the heat pump with the heating it replaces.

boiler_efficiency.name: Boiler efficiency
boiler_efficiency.description: Heat per kWh of gas billed: about 0.9 for a condensing boiler.

gas_standing_charge.name: Gas standing charge
gas_standing_charge.description: The gas connection's yearly standing charge, saved once it goes.

fill_year.name: Fill the year
fill_year.description: Fill the days the recorder lacks from recorded days with a similar sun. Off: scale the recorded days to a year.

not_loaded.message: Solar Energy Insights is not set up or not loaded.

needs_solar_counter.message: The scenario needs the solar energy counter: set it in the options.

needs_temperature.message: A heat pump needs the outdoor temperature: set a thermometer with statistics in the options.

too_little_history.message: The recorder holds less than a week of solar and house use; try again later.

better_reserve.title: A better reserve sensor is available

confirm.title: Use the effective reserve
confirm.description: The reserve now comes from {current}, PowerOcean's plain limit, which can read 0 % while the EcoFlow app keeps a higher backup reserve. {better} is the higher of the two: with it, the plan never counts on energy the battery will not give. Switch to it?

init.description: {energy} looks like your {name}'s energy counter. Add it as an appliance? The tonight card can then show what running it would leave, without counting its past runs twice. You can change its figures afterwards under the integration's appliances.
